title: finding(tooling): the citation census counts a phantom final line — `split(LF)` makes every trailing-newline file read one line longer than it is
body:
`scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` computes a cited file's length as `text.split(LF).length`. A file that ends in a newline therefore yields a **phantom final empty line**, so the census believes every such file is one line longer than it is.

Dedup keywords: `cross-file-line-citation-census` · off-by-one · `split(LF)` phantom line · `wc -l` 808 vs census 809 · out-of-range boundary · phantom trailing line

⛔ Not claimed, not dispatched. ⛔ No labels set here — the filing seat does not grade.

## Measured, on `origin/main`, by the filing seat

`scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`:

| reading | value |
|:--|--:|
| `wc -c` | **39757** |
| LF characters (`tr -cd '\n' \| wc -c`) | **808** |
| `wc -l` | **808** |
| `text.split(LF).length` | **809** |
| last split element | **the empty string** |

⚠️ **A correction to the hand-back this was filed from**, stated rather than smoothed: the `os-dev` round that found this reported **38980 bytes** for the same file, measured at ref `a0176176a`. On `origin/main` at filing time it reads **39757**. The LF count, `wc -l` and the split length are identical, so **the finding is unaffected** — ⛔ but the byte figure is a reading of a ref, not a property of the file, and inheriting it would have published a number this seat did not take.

## The consequence, and why it is small but exactly on-topic

The printed `file has N lines` is **wrong by one on every trailing-newline file** — which is nearly all of them. And a citation pointing AT the phantom line is scored `non-substantive` (it reads the empty string) instead of `out-of-range`.

⭐ **Both verdicts are false, so no headline count moves.** This is not a correctness emergency. It is filed because **an off-by-one in a line-counting instrument is the subject of objectui#9865 one level up**: an instrument that cannot be checked against a simpler reading of the same quantity is an instrument a reader has to trust.

## ⛔ Why it was deliberately NOT repaired in objectui#9865's round

Moving the boundary moves the `out-of-range` / `non-substantive` split — **the very numbers that card exists to make readable**. Repairing it inside that round would have made its before/after population figures incomparable. ⇒ separate card, on purpose.

## What would falsify this card

`split(LF).length` is the intended definition of 「lines」 here and something downstream depends on the phantom element ⇒ close it, and say what depends on it. ⛔ The filing seat did **not** audit every consumer of that length.
